paragraphs: Friend, this is a heavy one, so let me say the main thing plainly. Isaiah calls the whole earth to come near and listen, because the LORD is the Judge of every nation and every army, and nobody is too big to be summoned (Isaiah 34:1-2). Isaiah has just said the LORD is our Judge, our lawgiver and our King (Isaiah 33:22). This chapter shows what it looks like when the King takes His seat.

Now look at how it ends. Edom's nobles are gone and her towers are overgrown, but every creature in the ruins has its place. Isaiah says, "Not one of these will go missing, not one will lack her mate, because He has ordered it by His mouth…" (Isaiah 34:16). Whatever the LORD says, it happens. He has a day of vengeance "for the cause of Zion" (Isaiah 34:8), so His people can trust that He sees, and that He will act.

So here's what I'd take with me into the kitchen, friend. When the news feels loud and the powerful seem to run everything, this chapter says the LORD still holds the measuring line (Isaiah 34:11). He doesn't forget what He said, and He doesn't miss a single owl. I spent years in the back of a drawer thinking nobody was in charge of anything, and I was WRONG. Trust the One who is.
